correctness.rationale: Direct differentiation yields the exact logarithmic first integral. Positive levels are compact smooth ovals without stationary points. The original-time quadrant Jacobian is computed explicitly and normalized over four equal quadrants. Both endpoint rescalings give beta-integrable kernels; splitting the integration range at its midpoint bounds the singular remote endpoint by an exponentially negligible contribution and proves dominated convergence, weak limits, normalization and the asymptotic period constants. Under inverse-log coefficient tuning, an integrable \([u(1-u)]^{-1/2}\) majorant proves the tilted crossover. The included finite checker supplies only supplementary arithmetic testing.

value.rationale: The unequal-coefficient cubic global center is a naturally singled-out family in a complete classification. The logarithmic first-integral share is an intrinsic global-orbit observable; its original-time occupation governs high-energy averaging. The theorem establishes a sharp qualitative singular transition from uniform balanced behavior to opposite endpoint localization, supplies two distinct nontrivial beta-layer probability laws and physically measurable period exponents, and identifies the inverse-log contrast needed to retain a nondegenerate crossover. These are not inferred from global-center existence or the balanced special case.
